p6_b1.ocr: In the study, the Phototype II group consisted of 10 participants, with a sex distribution of 2 males and 8 females, while the Phototype V group had 6 participants, comprising 4 males and 2 females. The average age for Phototype II participants was 45 ± 9 years, whereas for Phototype V, it was 38 ± 11 years. Both groups had a body mass index (BMI) of 26 ± 4 kg m−2 for Phototype II and 26 ± 3 kg m−2 for Phototype V. The minimum erythemal dose (MED) was significantly lower in Phototype II at 37 ± 13 mJ cm−2, compared to 146 ± 64 mJ cm−2 in Phototype V. Baseline parathyroid hormone (PTH) levels were recorded at 2.3 ± 0.9 pmol L−1 for Phototype II and 3.8 ± 1.7 pmol L−1 for Phototype V.

p6_b2.ocr: Final PTH levels decreased to 2.3 ± 0.7 pmol L−1 in Phototype II and were 3.1 ± 1.2 pmol L−1 in Phototype V. Dietary vitamin D intake during week 1 was 3.1 ± 2.7 μg per day for Phototype II and 2.6 ± 2.5 μg per day for Phototype V, while week 6 intake was 3.3 ± 2.6 μg per day for Phototype II and 2.0 ± 1.4 μg per day for Phototype V. Baseline 25-hydroxyvitamin D (25(OH)D) levels were 36.5 ± 13.0 nmol L−1 for Phototype II and 17.2 ± 6.3 nmol L−1 for Phototype V, with final levels at 54.3 ± 10.5 nmol L−1 for Phototype II and 25.5 ± 9.5 nmol L−1 for Phototype V.
